A.notes: Site A has a clear brick/courtyard/light idea, and the hero plus project drawings make the studio's identity legible immediately. The scroll-frame strip suggests a purposeful step-through of the five projects and then studio/process/contact, while the reduced-motion version keeps content present and usable. Typography and illustration are strong, though the motion-enabled full-page capture shows some awkward empty stretches that keep it just short of top craft.

B.notes: Site B has an elegant plan-led system and refined typography, with strong diagrams and a calm editorial structure. But the default motion version opens on a largely empty first screen and appears to hide the main positioning line; in the scroll frames that reads as broken rather than useful storytelling. The reduced-motion version is clearer than the default, so Motion and Craft score notably lower despite solid accessibility checks.

raw.why: A carries the brief's identity and story more consistently, while B's default motion undermines an otherwise strong design.
